reason: This passage from Judges 4 demonstrates Yahweh's active intervention to help the Hebrew people. When the Israelites cry out (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־ יְהוָה), God responds through the prophetess Deborah with explicit promises: 'the Lord will deliver Sisera into your hand' (וּנְתַתִּ֖יהוּ בְּיָדֶֽךָ). Throughout the narrative, Yahweh actively fights for Israel—He 'discomfits' (יָהָם) Sisera's forces, 'subdues' (וַיַּכְנַ֤ע) King Jabin, and strengthens Israel's hand until they destroy their oppressor (וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ יַ֤ד בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָל֣וֹךְ וְקָשָׁ֔ה). The text shows a clear pattern: oppression → Israel cries out → God delivers them. This demonstrates that helping the Hebrew people is definitively one of Yahweh's operative goals in this narrative.
